evidence.observation: Retention/prune entry point that decides which lifecycle edges out of the current status are allowed. For each owned project it computes `terminalStatus = status === 'success' || status === 'failed' || status === 'fail'`, `terminalExpired` (>= FINAL_PROJECT_RETENTION_MS since projectTimestamp), `restoredExpired` (status 'archived', restoredAt > 0, >= RESTORED_PROJECT_RETENTION_MS) and `archivedNeedsUnload` (status 'archived', restoredAt === 0, at least one member agent currently loaded). If none of the three gates hold, the project goes to `skipped`/`kept` and no transition is attempted (line 177-180). Only when a gate holds is `wattclaw.team.project.archive` called (line 186), and a cold archived project whose agents are not loaded is reported as archived without any RPC (line 182-185). So the allowed edges are terminal->archived (after 3 days), restored-archived->archived (after 24h) and loaded cold-archived->archived; every non-terminal status (planning/in_progress/pending/creating/waiting/paused) and every not-yet-expired terminal status has a forbidden edge into archived.

Status normalization used by the state machine: the raw project status is trimmed and lower-cased, and a non-string/missing status becomes ''. This makes the alias edge explicit (e.g. 'FAILED'/'Failed'/'fail' all collapse to 'failed') and means an unknown status string can never match the terminal or archived gates, hence it is retained.

Window constants that parameterize the allowed edges: FINAL_PROJECT_RETENTION_MS = 3 days (terminal -> archived), RESTORED_PROJECT_RETENTION_MS = 24 hours (restored archived -> archived), SHANGHAI_UTC_OFFSET_MS = UTC+8 (retention clock). A terminal project inside the 3-day window, or a restored archived project inside the 24-hour window, is a forbidden edge and is kept.

The sanctioned reverse edge archived -> active/restored. It lists gateway agents, re-registers only the members whose agentId is missing via `wattclaw.team.project.member.update` (carrying name/role/soul/skills/models), re-lists agents, throws 'WattClaw agents were not restored: ...' if any project agent is still absent, and returns `restored: projectStatus(currentProject) === 'archived'`. Restore is therefore an agent-materialization edge, not an arbitrary status write.

Schedules the daily evaluation of the lifecycle edges at 18:00 Asia/Shanghai (UTC+8) and rolls to the next day when the computed instant is not in the future. This fixes the granularity at which expired terminal/restored-archived projects are allowed to cross into archived.

The explicit project lifecycle state machine table, keyed by TARGET status with the list of allowed SOURCE statuses: planning:[pending,failed,in_progress,success,retrying]; in_progress:[planning,failed,success,retrying]; failed:[planning,in_progress,creating,pausing,resuming,retrying]; success:[in_progress]; pending:[retrying,creating]; creating:[waiting]; waiting:[creating]; pausing:[]; paused:[pausing,retrying]; resuming:[]; retrying:[failed]; archived:[]. The empty arrays are the forbidden edges: no status-update edge can enter pausing, resuming or archived.

Human-readable rendering of the same machine using 'A <= B|C' notation, which denotes allowed INCOMING edges B->A (not A->B): 'planning <= pending|failed|in_progress|success|retrying; in_progress <= planning|failed|success|retrying; failed <= planning|in_progress|creating|pausing|resuming|retrying; success <= in_progress; retrying <= failed; pending <= retrying; paused <= pausing|retrying'. It matches u_e except that it omits creating->pending, and it is only used for error messages and the tool description, so it is documentation rather than enforcement.

Call site that enforces the machine: identical status returns the project untouched (self-loop no-op, line begins `if(i===o)return ...`), then `dH(target)` validates the target against the set {planning,in_progress,success,failed,retrying,creating,waiting}, and `fH(current,target)` checks membership via `u_e[target].includes(current)`. Failures throw gH/pH errors naming the allowed target statuses and transition rules, and success persists `status: target, lastStatus: current`.

Client-side mirror of the forbidden edge guard: for `wattclaw.team.project.updated` it ignores a project already tracked as archived unless the incoming status is itself 'archived' (`if (archivedProjectIds.has(targetProjectId) && nextStatus !== 'archived') return`), so realtime events cannot move archived -> non-archived; that reverse edge must go through the explicit restore path.

UI edge into archived: it calls `archiveWattClawProject`, records the id in `archivedProjectIds`, forces `project.status = 'archived'` and clears `runtimeReady`, i.e. archiving is an explicit user action routed through the dedicated RPC (the same RPC the runtime prune logic uses), not through the status-update state machine.

UI reverse edge archived -> 'restored': only when the current status is 'archived' does it call activateWattClawProject, strip the project from `archivedProjectIds` and set `status: 'restored'`; the initialize() path intentionally does NOT auto-restore archived projects. This confirms archived -> active is allowed only through the explicit activation edge.

Declared project status vocabulary: 'creating' | 'waiting' | 'pending' | 'planning' | 'in_progress' | 'paused' | 'failed' | 'archived' (plus arbitrary string). Note that 'success' and 'retrying', used by the state machine table, are absent from this union, and 'paused' is a declared status that the enforced table makes a dead end (incoming only from pausing/retrying, no outgoing edges except its own self-loop).

claims.claim: The runtime allows exactly three edges whose target is 'archived': terminal success/failed/fail -> archived after FINAL_PROJECT_RETENTION_MS (3 days, measured by projectTimestamp over updatedAt/createdAt), restored archived (restoredAt > 0) -> archived after RESTORED_PROJECT_RETENTION_MS (24h), and cold archived (restoredAt === 0) -> archived when at least one member agent is still loaded; the first two are the only ones that actually issue wattclaw.team.project.archive.

Every other edge into 'archived' is forbidden by pruneWattClawProjectsForUser: non-terminal statuses (pending/planning/creating/waiting/in_progress/paused and any unknown status) and terminal statuses still inside the 3-day window, plus restored archived projects still inside the 24-hour window, are pushed to skipped/kept and never receive an archive RPC; a cold archived project with no loaded agents is reported as archived but also receives no RPC.

The reverse edge archived -> active/restored is allowed only through activateWattClawProjectRuntime, which re-registers missing member agents with wattclaw.team.project.member.update, verifies the refreshed agents.list, throws when agents remain unloaded, and signals the transition with restored: true when the pre-activation status was 'archived'; status strings are normalized by projectStatus (trim + lowercase), so 'FAILED'/'fail' are aliases of 'failed' and the retention clock runs daily at 18:00 Asia/Shanghai.

The plugin's explicit lifecycle table u_e is target-keyed and defines the allowed incoming edges planning<-{pending,failed,in_progress,success,retrying}, in_progress<-{planning,failed,success,retrying}, failed<-{planning,in_progress,creating,pausing,resuming,retrying}, success<-{in_progress}, pending<-{retrying,creating}, creating<-{waiting}, waiting<-{creating}, paused<-{pausing,retrying}, retrying<-{failed}; its empty entries (pausing, resuming, archived) are forbidden targets, so no status-update edge can enter archived, pausing or resuming.

Enforcement of that machine happens in Ci via dH(target) (target restricted to planning|in_progress|success|failed|retrying|creating|waiting) plus fH(current,target) = u_e[target].includes(current), with identical status treated as a no-op; the gS() rule string ('A <= B|C' = incoming edge B->A) is only used for error text and the tool description, omits creating->pending, and must not be read as source->target edges.

Concrete forbidden edges follow from the two gates: archived->any (archived never appears as a source), paused->any except a paused self-loop (paused is a dead end), any->pausing/resuming/archived, success->failed, planning->success, pending->in_progress and pending->success, and success/pending are never valid sources for in_progress/planning except where u_e lists them (success->planning is allowed, pending->planning is allowed).

The client keeps the same edge discipline: handleRealtimeEvent ignores realtime updates that would move a project out of archived, archiveProject() is the only UI action that sets status 'archived' (via the archive RPC), and restoreProject() is the explicit archived -> 'restored' edge; the declared WattClawProjectStatus vocabulary omits 'success' and 'retrying' and makes 'paused' a declared but dead-end status.

conclusion: Two layers define project lifecycle edges in WattClaw, and they must not be conflated. (1) The enforced status machine (plugins/wattclaw-team/dist/index.js, u_e + dH/fH in Ci) is target-keyed: 'A <= B|C' in the gS() description means incoming edges B->A, not A->B. Allowed edges are pending->planning, failed->planning, in_progress->planning, success->planning, retrying->planning; planning->in_progress, failed->in_progress, success->in_progress, retrying->in_progress; planning|in_progress|creating|pausing|resuming|retrying->failed; in_progress->success; failed->retrying; waiting->creating; creating->waiting; pausing->paused and retrying->paused; retrying->pending and creating->pending. Forbidden edges are everything not in that relation, notably any->archived (u_e.archived = []), any->pausing/resuming (empty source lists), archived->anything (archived is terminal: it never appears as a source), paused->anything except its own self-loop, success->failed, planning->success, pending->in_progress, and any transition into 'paused' other than from pausing/retrying; identical-status updates are no-ops, and target validity additionally rejects pending/paused/pausing/resuming/archived. (2) The runtime retention layer (server/services/wattclaw-project-runtime.js) is the only actor that actually writes 'archived', and it allows just three edges into archived: terminal success/failed/fail -> archived after the 3-day FINAL_PROJECT_RETENTION_MS window (projectTimestamp = updatedAt else createdAt), restored archived (restoredAt > 0) -> archived after the 24-hour RESTORED_PROJECT_RETENTION_MS window, and cold archived (restoredAt === 0) -> archived only when a member agent is still loaded; non-terminal statuses, unexpired terminal ones, and unexpired restored ones are forbidden and end in kept/skipped, while a cold archived project with no loaded agents is kept without any RPC. The sanctioned reverse edge archived -> active/restored is activateWattClawProjectRuntime, which re-materializes only missing members via wattclaw.team.project.member.update and throws if any agent stays unloaded. The frontend mirrors the discipline: realtime project.updated events cannot leave archived, archiveProject()/restoreProject() are the explicit archive and restore edges. Practical consequence: archiving is unreachable through the status-update path by design, and the plugin's 'paused'/'pausing'/'resuming' states are declared but effectively dead ends in the enforced table.

validation.notes: The repository has no node_modules and no vitest binary, so the official test suite (server/services/wattclaw-project-runtime.test.js) could not be executed and no dependency was installed. Substitute validation of limited strength was used: (a) `node --check server/services/wattclaw-project-runtime.js` parsed the required source without syntax errors; (b) a static assertion script re-read .prale-eval/result.json, confirmed task_id===28, repository==='wattclaw', mode==='explore', the presence of evidence/claims/conclusion/validation, verified that each evidence symbol literal actually occurs inside its inclusive start_line..end_line in the named file (including the minified dist where gS/u_e and Ci are on lines 932 and 934), that every claim's evidence_paths are non-empty and exist, and that the required path server/services/wattclaw-project-runtime.js has at least one substantive claim; (c) the u_e table and gS rule string text were asserted to be present verbatim in plugins/wattclaw-team/dist/index.js, and the retention gates in pruneWattClawProjectsForUser were asserted to be present in the required file. This is static/structural evidence only and is not equivalent to running the vitest suite; behavior under the real gateway RPC was not executed.
